nodes.name: Periphyton
nodes.desc: A living mat of algae and microbes on submerged plants and surfaces. In the Everglades it grows where sawgrass is sparse and feeds larval insects and amphibians.

nodes.name: Sawgrass
nodes.desc: Dominates the marshes and grows best in slow-moving water. Dense stands hold few animals, but alligators nest in them.

nodes.name: Waterlilies and bladderwort
nodes.desc: Submerged and floating plants of the open sloughs that give food and cover to aquatic animals.

nodes.name: Slough crayfish
nodes.desc: A crayfish that grazes on plants and microbes, and survives the dry season in burrows and wet refuges. Many wading birds, fish and mammals eat it.

nodes.name: Florida apple snail
nodes.desc: A large freshwater snail that grazes on algae and plants. It is nearly the only food of the snail kite.

nodes.name: Sailfin molly
nodes.desc: A small fish that grazes algae and plant matter. It is a staple prey for wading birds and larger fish.

nodes.name: Marsh rabbit
nodes.desc: A grass-eating rabbit of wet prairies and hammock edges. Pythons have sharply cut its numbers where they are established.

nodes.name: Eastern mosquitofish
nodes.desc: A tiny generalist that eats zooplankton, insects, and detritus. Bass, catfish and bluegill eat it, and so do wading birds.

nodes.name: Largemouth bass
nodes.desc: A fish predator of sloughs and canals that eats small fish and crayfish.

nodes.name: Limpkin
nodes.desc: A wading bird that specializes in extracting apple snails from their shells.

nodes.name: Snail kite
nodes.desc: A raptor whose diet is almost all apple snails. The Everglades kite is endangered, and drought or loss of snails hurts it.

nodes.name: Great Egret
nodes.desc: A tall wader that stalks fish, frogs, crayfish and insects in shallow water. It also takes young alligators.

nodes.name: Wood stork
nodes.desc: An endangered wader that feeds on fish concentrated in drying pools. Pythons have been found to eat storks.

nodes.name: Raccoon
nodes.desc: An omnivore of hammocks and marsh edges that eats crayfish, snails and eggs. Reported sightings fell sharply where pythons are established.

nodes.name: American alligator
nodes.desc: Digs gator holes that keep water through the dry season, giving fish and other animals a refuge. An opportunistic top predator.

nodes.name: Burmese python
nodes.desc: An invasive constrictor released from the pet trade. It eats mammals and birds, and has caused steep declines in medium-sized mammals.

nodes.name: Florida panther
nodes.desc: A rare big cat that hunts deer, hogs, raccoons and other mammals. Pythons eat the same prey.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm, bright shallow water drives year-round algal and plant growth.

nodes.name: Seasonal flooding
nodes.desc: Rain from May to October spreads water over the marsh. In the dry season it retreats to sloughs and gator holes.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Lightning fires, mostly in the wet season, and deep peat fires in dry spells renew sawgrass marshes.

nodes.name: Peat soil
nodes.desc: Slowly built organic soil in which marsh plants root.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.
